speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Ministry keeps track of how many adult persons with special needs or persons with disability are financially dependent on their parents who have retired; (b) what are the current programmes and schemes available to help adult persons with special needs or disabilities to secure their own livelihood for their financial self-sufficiency, in particular those who are high functioning; and (c) what is the success rate of these programmes and schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: SG Enable offers a wide variety of support for PwDs seeking employment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the Open Door Programme (ODP), PwDs receive up to one year of job matching and customised employment support from trained job coaches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Grants under the ODP provide subsidies for PwDs to attend training courses by the Enabling Academy – SG Enable's disability learning hub – as well as for workshops that prepare employers and their employees without disabilities to interact with, hire, integrate and retain employees with disabilities in their organisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: PwDs can also take up job and training opportunities created under the customised Place-and-Train and Attach-and-Train programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: More than 380 job and training opportunities have been filled under these two programmes since they were introduced in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government also provides employers with wage support through the Enabling Employment Credit (EEC).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: More support is provided to encourage the hiring of PwDs who are long-term unemployed and are more likely to be financially reliant on their families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Employers who hire PwDs who have not been working for at least six months will receive an additional 20% of wage offsets, capped at $400 per month per employee, for the first nine months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In 2022, close to 6,600 organisations received the EEC and collectively employed more than 10,000 employees with disabilities, including close to 2,000 who had not been in work for at least six months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Workfare Income Supplement also provides additional support to lower-income workers, including PwDs, by supplementing their income and Central Provident Fund savings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Building an inclusive workplace requires a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As part of the Enabling Masterplan 2030, we encourage more employers to provide suitable employment opportunities for PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Later this year, the first Enabling Business Hub (EBH) will be launched to bring jobs and employment support closer to where PwDs live.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the answer.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is quite heartening to hear that we have been making progress.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that since December last year, we have 35,500 students with special needs who are in our education system right now, which means that they will be growing up to become adults in the next 10 to 15 years.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Given that we are making some progress, are there going to be further investments in ensuring that this whole-of-society approach can be accelerated to further enable more numbers of persons with special needs to be employed in their adulthood, to greater success, meaning, more retention and to measure their level of self-sufficiency, because this is likely to be a cost to the country?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: And whether, in the long term, do we look at the support and integration of persons with special needs based on a certain ratio of welfare versus self-sufficiency target?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: There are some who may not be able to work.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: But among those who can, with the relevant training and the relevant sensitisation of the employers and the general public, can we move that needle further and faster?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The short answer to what she is asking about, essentially, is yes, more will be done.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The EBH that I spoke about earlier is the first, the pilot.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Today, the industries that are more amenable include services, food and beverages.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As I mentioned in my main reply, we are trying to move into other new growth areas, blue oceans for PwDs, such as logistics.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To achieve the aspirations that we want for PwDs, I think we need to go beyond the tangibles, we need to go beyond programmes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Essentially, we are also talking about a change of mindsets, a change of hearts as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We do need a change of hearts on multiple fronts.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: First of all, for PwDs themselves, many of them would also have this question in their minds, especially if they have not been in the workplace for a long time, "Can I do it, can I be an employee of an organisation, a business, a corporate?" That is the question we need to address.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: They will ask, "Can my loved ones do it?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Will he or she be bullied?" These are concerns we need to address as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Most of all, I would say, beyond the C-suite consent or support that we get from industries, we do need every employee, every supervisor – or as many of them as we can – to really embrace the fact that PwDs can live amongst us, can also be my fellow employee, can be my fellow workmate.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Tracking data will ensure that there is better financial security for all adults with disabilities in our country, just like we would encourage typical folks to do the same as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think that there is a need to gauge the size of the monster, the issue.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There should be an intentional approach to first determine the archetypes of adults with disabilities – some can work full-time, some can work part-time, some will need more care and cannot really work in open employment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And then, there are also the family archetypes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are different types of families – some can afford, very much they have their own resources —

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think I will summarise it into two parts.
